name: OpenAI API
headline: Industry standard LLMs with tiered TPM/RPM rate limits and per-token pricing
pricing_model: Usage-based (per 1M tokens)
free_tier: None for API (Only $5 initial credit for some new accounts, expires in 3 months)
hidden_costs: Heavy TPM (Tokens Per Minute) tier locks require depositing hundreds of dollars in prepay to upgrade limits
Batch API is 50% cheaper but has 24h latency SLA
Fine-tuning storage and hosting fees accumulate automatically
pros: Highest intelligence benchmarks
Vast ecosystem & SDK compatibility
Structured JSON outputs
cons: Expensive reasoning tokens (o1/o3)
Aggressive rate limits on lower tiers
best_for: Production apps requiring state-of-the-art multi-step reasoning

name: Anthropic Claude API
headline: Elite coding & long-context frontier models (Claude 3.5 Sonnet / Haiku)
pricing_model: Usage-based (per 1M tokens)
free_tier: $5 free credit upon phone verification
hidden_costs: 200K context window gets expensive rapidly if Prompt Caching is not implemented
Prompt caching requires exact prefix matching and charges 10% premium for writes
Haiku 3.5 price was increased 4x compared to legacy Haiku 3
pros: Unmatched code generation & editing capability
Massive 200k context window
90% discount on cached tokens
cons: Strict tier graduation requiring high monthly spend
Occasional capacity overload during peak US hours
best_for: Software development agents, document parsing, and complex coding workflows

name: DeepSeek API
headline: Disruptive open-weights reasoning model at 95% discount vs Western rivals
pricing_model: Usage-based (Cache Hit: $0.07/M, Output: $2.19/M for R1)
free_tier: 5M free tokens for new accounts
hidden_costs: Frequent peak-hour 429 / 503 rate limits due to overwhelming global demand
Output token generation for R1 deep thinking can be 5x-10x longer than standard LLMs
Requires third-party fallback (OpenRouter/Groq) for production uptime
pros: 1/10th to 1/20th the price of OpenAI o1
Extreme reasoning benchmark scores
Full OpenAI SDK compatibility
cons: API stability can wobble during US trading hours
Server capacity bottlenecks
best_for: Budget-conscious solo developers, batch processing, and offline research

name: Groq LPU Inference
headline: Ultra-fast hardware inference (500+ tokens/sec) for Llama 3 & open models
pricing_model: Usage-based / Enterprise provisioned throughput
free_tier: Generous free tier (up to 30 requests/min on Llama 3.3 70B)
hidden_costs: Free tier is subject to strict daily token ceilings (e.g. 100k-500k tokens/day)
Paid on-demand tier jumps directly into credit card billing
Only supports open-source architectures (Llama, Gemma, Mixtral)
pros: Instantaneous real-time responses
Sub-second voice and interactive agent latency
Compatible with OpenAI client
cons: Context limits lower than Claude
No proprietary frontier models
best_for: Voice agents, real-time autocomplete, and ultra-low latency bots

name: Supabase
headline: Open source Firebase alternative built on dedicated PostgreSQL instances
pricing_model: Monthly tier + Overages (Compute hours + Egress + Storage)
free_tier: 2 free projects, 500MB database, 1GB storage, 2GB bandwidth (pauses after 7 days of inactivity)
hidden_costs: Database automatically pauses on Free tier after 1 week without active queries
Storage egress is $0.09/GB after included 50GB on Pro
Point-in-time recovery (PITR) requires an extra $100/mo add-on
Compute instance upgrade starts at $10/mo to $640/mo per project
pros: Full native Postgres with pgvector support
Instant Auth, Realtime, and Edge Functions
Self-hostable with Docker
cons: Multiple projects require separate $25/mo Pro plans
Egress bills can spike from image hosting
best_for: Full-stack indie SaaS, AI apps needing vector search, and rapid MVPs

name: Neon Serverless Postgres
headline: Serverless Postgres with autoscaling, database branching, and zero-scale idle
pricing_model: Compute unit hours (CU) + Storage GB-months + Written data
free_tier: 0.5GB data storage, 1 project, 100 CU compute hours/month
hidden_costs: Cold start latency (~500ms - 1s) when database wakes up from 0 compute units
Synthetic data writes (logs/migrations) consume monthly written data quotas
Branching data inherits storage costs if modified heavily
pros: Branch database like git branches for preview deployments
Autoscales compute based on load
Scales to zero to save idle cost
cons: Cold start can annoy users if not using connection pooling
No built-in Auth (DB only)
best_for: Serverless Next.js/Vercel apps, multi-tenant databases, staging branches

name: Google Firebase
headline: Google's NoSQL real-time document database & mobile app backend
pricing_model: Per read, write, and delete operations in Cloud Firestore
free_tier: 1GB storage, 50k reads/day, 20k writes/day
hidden_costs: The infamous 'Infinite Loop Read Disaster': an un-memoized React hook can trigger millions of reads and a $1,000+ overnight bill
Blaze plan has no hard billing spend cap, only alerts
Complex queries require manual compound indexes or third-party Algolia ($$$)
pros: Bulletproof 99.999% uptime backed by Google
Instant mobile SDKs for iOS/Android
Zero server maintenance
cons: Catastrophic surprise bills from read loops
Vendor lock-in to Google NoSQL architecture
best_for: Mobile games, real-time chat apps, and prototypes needing Google auth

name: Vercel
headline: The premier frontend cloud platform for Next.js and modern web frameworks
pricing_model: Per seat ($20/mo) + Fast Data Transfer ($0.15/GB) + Fast Compute
free_tier: 100GB bandwidth, serverless execution limits, strictly non-commercial use only
hidden_costs: Hobby tier terms officially ban commercial sites (monetized blogs/SaaS)
Fast Data Transfer overage is $0.15/GB (10x Cloudflare rates)
Edge Function execution duration overages hit quickly on unoptimized SSR
Every added GitHub collaborator automatically incurs a $20/mo seat charge
pros: Best-in-class Next.js developer experience
Instant preview branches for PRs
Global edge caching network
cons: High overage prices for bandwidth & functions
Mandatory seat pricing for teams
best_for: Next.js frontend applications, venture-backed startups, high-margin SaaS

name: Cloudflare Pages & Workers
headline: Edge computing and global static site hosting with zero egress fees
pricing_model: Requests + CPU time (ZERO egress bandwidth fees)
free_tier: Unlimited bandwidth, 500 builds/month, 100k Workers requests/day
hidden_costs: Edge runtime does not support standard Node.js native binary packages without polyfills
KV and D1 database operations incur write unit charges on huge traffic spikes
Build limits on free tier cap at 20 minutes per deployment
pros: Zero bandwidth egress fees forever
Cheapest edge computing on earth ($5/mo for 10M requests)
Unrivaled DDoS protection
cons: Node.js ecosystem compatibility hurdles
Developer dashboard has steep learning curve
best_for: pSEO programmatic sites, static sites, high-traffic APIs, and cost-conscious founders

name: Railway
headline: Instant infrastructure platform to deploy full-stack apps, Docker containers, and databases
pricing_model: Exact vCPU & RAM usage per minute ($0.000463/GB-hour)
free_tier: $5 one-time credit (no permanent free tier)
hidden_costs: Background worker memory leaks will quietly max out RAM and inflate monthly usage bills
Outbound network egress is $0.10/GB
No free tier: trial credit expires and requires adding a credit card
pros: Deploy any Dockerfile or GitHub repo in 30 seconds
One-click templates for Redis, Postgres, n8n
Transparent per-second resource billing
cons: Costs scale linearly with memory/CPU without auto-scale down to zero
Not ideal for pure static frontends
best_for: Python backends, Node/Express APIs, background cron workers, and self-hosted tools

name: Render
headline: Modern cloud alternative to Heroku for web apps, background workers, and Postgres
pricing_model: Fixed monthly instance pricing + Outbound bandwidth overages ($0.10/GB)
free_tier: Free web services spin down after 15 minutes of inactivity; free Postgres expires after 30 days
hidden_costs: Free PostgreSQL database is strictly deleted after 30 days if not upgraded to $7/mo
Spin-up time for idle free web services takes 50+ seconds
Static sites are free, but web servers require dedicated $7/mo minimum per instance
pros: Predictable flat monthly billing
Simple Heroku migration path
Native private networking between services
cons: Slow free tier cold starts
Free database expiration catch
best_for: Small SaaS backends, Rails/Django apps, and developers wanting fixed monthly budgets

name: Zapier
headline: The market leader in no-code app integrations with 7,000+ supported apps
pricing_model: Tiered task count (billed annually or 33% monthly premium)
free_tier: 100 tasks/month, 5 single-step Zaps only
hidden_costs: Every single step in a multi-step Zap consumes 1 task (a 5-step automation with 200 runs consumes 1,000 tasks and triggers high overage fees)
Webhooks and filtering require paid plans
Monthly billing has a heavy 33% markup over advertised annual price
Auto-replay on failed tasks requires higher tier plans
pros: Massive ecosystem: connects to virtually every business tool on earth
Extremely polished and reliable trigger system
No-code AI actions
cons: Extremely expensive at scale ($300+/mo for modest volumes)
Multi-step task multiplier burns credits fast
best_for: Non-technical founders, sales operations, and connecting obscure CRM tools

name: Make (Integromat)
headline: Visual automation platform with drag-and-drop data manipulation at 1/5th Zapier's price
pricing_model: Operations volume (1 operation = 1 module execution)
free_tier: 1,000 operations/month, 2 active scenarios
hidden_costs: Data iteration loops (e.g. processing 100 rows in a sheet) execute 100 individual operations in seconds
High frequency polling intervals require Pro plans
Large file transfers can trigger execution payload limits
pros: Visual flow-chart builder with advanced router branching
10,000 operations for $9 vs Zapier's 750 tasks for $30
Deep JSON manipulation & array aggregators
cons: Steeper learning curve than Zapier
Debugging complex errors can take time
best_for: Agencies, power users, growth hackers, and complex data pipeline automations

name: n8n (Self-Hosted & Cloud)
headline: Fair-code workflow automation tool with unlimited self-hosted executions
pricing_model: Execution-based on Cloud / $0 for infinite runs when self-hosted via Docker
free_tier: Self-hosted Community Edition is 100% free with unlimited workflows and executions
hidden_costs: Self-hosting requires maintaining a $5/mo VPS (Railway/Hetzner) and configuring SSL/backups
Community edition restricts enterprise user roles and multi-tenancy
Cloud plan counts entire workflow executions, but charges overage per extra execution
pros: Unlimited automations for $0 when hosted on a cheap server
Native AI Agent nodes with LangChain integrations
Write raw JavaScript or Python anywhere
cons: Self-hosting maintenance & update responsibilities
Cloud tier is slightly pricey compared to Make
best_for: Developers, technical founders, and privacy-first teams with millions of automations

name: Notion
headline: All-in-one connected workspace for notes, docs, project management, and AI
pricing_model: Per user / per month (billed annually, or $12/mo monthly)
free_tier: Unlimited blocks for individuals, 5MB file upload limit, up to 10 guest collaborators
hidden_costs: Notion AI is NOT included in Plus plans: costs an additional $8-$10/user/month
Adding a full workspace member immediately triggers a monthly seat invoice
File uploads capped at 5MB on free tier
pros: Incredible relational databases and customizable views
Vast template ecosystem & API integrations
Generous free tier for solo creators
cons: Seat fees multiply quickly for growing teams
Can feel sluggish on huge databases
best_for: Solo creators, early startups, company wikis, and project management

name: Airtable
headline: Relational database disguised as a collaborative spreadsheet for business operations
pricing_model: Per seat / per month + Record count limits per base
free_tier: 1,000 records per base, 1GB attachments, up to 5 editors
hidden_costs: Strict record limits: hitting 1,000 records on free forces an upgrade to $24/user/mo
Every person who edits a base requires a paid seat (no cheap viewer-editor distinction)
Syncing tables between bases consumes sync quotas
pros: World-class interface designer for internal business apps
Robust automation triggers and scripts
Extremely enterprise-friendly
cons: Brutally expensive seat fees for small teams
Hard record count ceilings
best_for: Internal operations, agency client portals, content production pipelines

name: Perplexity AI
headline: Conversational conversational answer engine replacing Google Search with live citations
pricing_model: Flat monthly subscription / API token usage
free_tier: Unlimited standard queries, 5 Pro searches per day
hidden_costs: API pricing for sonar models charges for both token count and search request frequency
Pro search rate limit during peak global breaking-news cycles
Third-party model switching (Claude 3.5 Sonnet) subject to internal token throttles
pros: Saves 2+ hours daily compared to traditional web search
Multi-model switching (Claude, GPT-4o, Sonar)
Upload and search local PDF files seamlessly
cons: Enterprise team seats require higher tiers
Occasionally hallucinates on niche technical code
best_for: Founders, researchers, investors, and content creators needing instant verified facts

name: Cursor AI Editor
headline: AI-first fork of VS Code with deep codebase indexing and multi-file composer
pricing_model: Monthly subscription (500 fast premium requests/mo + unlimited slow)
free_tier: 14-day Pro trial, then 50 slow requests/month
hidden_costs: Fast request limit: 500 fast requests burns out in ~10 days of heavy coding
Overages after 500 requests cost $0.10/request or waiting in slow queue
Custom API keys bypass 500 limit but pay full Anthropic API rates directly
pros: Codebase-wide semantic indexing and `@Codebase` context
Composer mode generates full features across multiple files
Zero-friction migration from VS Code extensions
cons: Can burn through 500 fast requests quickly on large refactors
Occasional cloud sync stalls
best_for: Full-stack engineers, solo developers, and fast-moving startup teams

name: GitHub Copilot
headline: The world's most widely deployed AI developer tool directly inside your IDE
pricing_model: Fixed monthly or annual seat billing
free_tier: 2,000 code completions and 50 chat requests per month
hidden_costs: Workspace-wide refactoring and deep multi-file editing is limited compared to Cursor
Business tier requires organization-wide GitHub Enterprise billing management
Copilot Workspace features locked behind waitlists or higher plans
pros: Predictable flat $10/mo with zero unexpected overages
Supported officially in VS Code, JetBrains, Neovim
Backed by GitHub Enterprise privacy guarantees
cons: Context awareness is shallower than Cursor
Less aggressive at full-project scaffolding
best_for: Corporate developers, security-conscious teams, and cost-predictable workflows

name: Fly.io
headline: Run full-stack apps and Docker containers globally close to your users
starting_price: $0 Free Allowance | Pay-as-you-go from $1.94/mo per VM
pricing_model: Micro-VM compute seconds + Persistent Volume Storage + Outbound data
free_tier: Free allowance covers small shared-cpu VMs (up to 3 shared-cpu-1x 256MB VMs)
hidden_costs: Requires credit card entry to activate account even for free allowance
Persistent volumes cannot be easily resized downward without migration
Dedicated IPv4 addresses cost $2/mo extra (IPv6 is free)
pros: Run apps physically close to users in 30+ edge regions
Deploy any Docker container seamlessly
True scale-to-zero capability with fast resume
cons: CLI-centric workflow without a beginner-friendly GUI
Storage volume management requires terminal skill
best_for: Elixir/Phoenix apps, SQLite on the edge, low-latency WebSocket backends

name: DigitalOcean App Platform & Droplets
headline: Simple cloud infrastructure and managed Kubernetes for growing developers
pricing_model: Fixed monthly tier per Droplet/Container + Bandwidth overages ($0.01/GB)
free_tier: 3 free static sites hosted on App Platform forever; $200 60-day credit for new users
hidden_costs: Bandwidth overage is cheap ($0.01/GB) but begins billing immediately if pooling threshold is breached
Managed databases start at $15/mo (far higher than basic $4 droplets)
Automatic weekly backup snapshots add 20% to droplet costs
pros: Extremely predictable fixed monthly billing
Vast library of community tutorials and guides
Free static site hosting with SSL
cons: Manual server maintenance required for plain Droplets
App Platform cold build times can lag
best_for: Self-hosting WordPress, n8n, Docker setups, and developers wanting fixed bills

name: PostHog
headline: The all-in-one product analytics suite with session replay, feature flags, and A/B tests
starting_price: $0 Free Tier | Pay-as-you-go based on event volume
pricing_model: Generous free volume tier + Decaying unit cost per million events
free_tier: 1,000,000 events/month, 5,000 session recordings/month, unlimited feature flags
hidden_costs: Session recording overages: exceeding 5,000 recordings can ramp up bills if sample rate isn't set
Billing alerts must be configured manually to prevent spikes from DDoS traffic tracking
Self-hosted version is no longer officially supported for new open-source installs
pros: Best free tier in the analytics industry (1M free events every month)
Replaces Mixpanel, Hotjar, and LaunchDarkly simultaneously
Built-in reverse proxy keeps ad-blockers from blocking analytics
cons: Dashboard can feel overwhelming due to sheer feature count
Session recording network payload
best_for: Indie SaaS founders, growth teams, and product managers wanting full visibility

name: Plausible Analytics
headline: Lightweight, open-source and privacy-friendly Google Analytics alternative
pricing_model: Monthly pageview tiers (annual discount available)
free_tier: 30-day free trial (no permanent free cloud tier)
hidden_costs: Going viral on Hacker News/Twitter can bump pageviews into a higher $19-$49/mo bracket
No free cloud tier after the 30-day trial expires
Advanced event funnels requires configuring custom properties
pros: Under 1KB tracking script (zero website slowdown)
100% GDPR, CCPA, and PECR compliant with no cookie banners needed
Ultra-clean single-page dashboard
cons: No session replay or heatmaps
Monthly subscription required for cloud hosting
best_for: Privacy-conscious blogs, pSEO sites, portfolio projects, and lean startups

name: Resend
headline: Modern transactional email API built for developers with React Email templates
pricing_model: Monthly email volume tier + Dedicated IP add-on ($30/mo)
free_tier: 3,000 emails/month, 100 emails/day limit, 1 sending domain
hidden_costs: Free tier enforces a hard 100 emails/day cap (stops bulk onboarding bursts)
Adding more than 1 domain requires upgrading to the $20/mo Pro tier
Dedicated IP for high deliverability costs an extra $30/month
pros: Design email templates directly using React & Tailwind (`react-email`)
Sub-100ms API response time
Cleanest developer dashboard in the email industry
cons: 100 emails/day free cap is tight for sudden traffic
Marketing broadcast features are still evolving
best_for: Next.js applications, indie founders sending transactional receipts & magic links

name: Postmark
headline: Legendary email service provider with the industry's highest transactional deliverability
pricing_model: Predictable monthly volume + Automatic pooled overage pricing
free_tier: 100 test emails forever (strictly for developer staging)
hidden_costs: Strict manual vetting process: new accounts undergo manual domain and compliance review
Separates transactional streams from broadcast marketing streams strictly to preserve reputation
No free production tier
pros: Fastest inbox delivery speeds in the world (consistently <5 seconds)
Detailed 45-day searchable email event logs
Unrivaled sender IP reputation
cons: More expensive per email than AWS SES or Resend
Strict account approval gating
best_for: Mission-critical password resets, billing invoices, and financial SaaS applications

name: Stripe
headline: The global standard infrastructure for internet commerce, billing, and payouts
pricing_model: Per-transaction percentage + Fixed flat fee
free_tier: No monthly setup or maintenance fees; only pay when you make sales
hidden_costs: International cards incur an extra +1.5% fee + 1% currency conversion fee
Stripe Billing (recurring subscription automation) charges an extra 0.5% - 0.8% on recurring volume
Stripe Tax automatically charges 0.5% per transaction if turned on
Dispute chargeback fee is $15 per lost chargeback
pros: Works in 46+ countries with local payment methods (Apple Pay, SEPA, iDEAL)
Stripe Checkout and Customer Portal require zero backend coding
Unmatched developer documentation and SDKs
cons: Fees accumulate silently with Tax + Billing + International add-ons (can reach 5%-6%)
Can freeze accounts under high chargeback ratios
best_for: Any online business, SaaS subscription, or e-commerce store with registered legal entity

name: Lemon Squeezy (Merchant of Record)
headline: All-in-one payment processing that acts as your Merchant of Record, handling global taxes
pricing_model: Per-transaction fee (Includes global sales tax & EU VAT compliance)
free_tier: No monthly fee, pay only upon making sales
hidden_costs: 5% + $0.50 is significantly higher than direct Stripe (2.9% + $0.30) on low-ticket items
Payout fee: international PayPal/Wise payouts incur small transfer fees
Acquired by Stripe in 2024; roadmap merging underway
pros: Acts as Merchant of Record: handles global EU VAT, GST, and US Sales Tax filing automatically
No need to register tax entities across multiple countries
Clean customer portal and license key generator
cons: Higher per-sale take rate
Undergoing integration shifts post-Stripe acquisition
best_for: Indie digital creators, software license sellers, and solo SaaS founders without accountants

name: Gumroad
headline: The simplest platform for creators and developers to sell digital products & kits online
starting_price: 10% flat fee per sale + payment processing fees
pricing_model: Flat 10% fee + Credit card/PayPal processing fee (~2.9% - 3.4% + $0.30)
free_tier: Free to list unlimited products, zero monthly subscription fees
hidden_costs: Total take rate reaches approximately 13% - 15% once credit card processing is included
Payout schedule: weekly payouts have rolling security reserves for new accounts
Custom CSS customization is minimal compared to self-hosted checkouts
pros: Absolute fastest zero-code setup in the world (live in 5 minutes)
Handles global EU VAT & tax compliance cleanly
Built-in affiliate system, discount codes, and customer email blasts
cons: 10% platform fee is high for large revenue volumes ($10k+/mo)
Branded Gumroad checkout overlay
best_for: Selling PDFs, Notion templates, code boilerplates, checklists, and digital kits
